male.name: The Sirsi arecanut farmer
male.tagline: Havyaka arecanut grower whose daughter's schooling hangs on bad roads, disease and harvest income.

dayInLife.text: Walks the plantation to check the areca palms and the drip lines from the check-dam.
Pollination and irrigation fill the dry months.
Disease-watch and harvest, then weeks of husking, boiling and sun-drying the nuts.
Does wage work on larger plantations, and hires migrant labour for a few weeks at his own peak.
Goes to Sirsi to sell produce, buy fertiliser and pesticide, and deal with CAMPCO and the cooperative bank.

topics.label: Daily Life & Work
topics.headline: Plantation rhythm set by monsoon, disease and cooperative prices
points: Arecanut, intercropped with pepper and cocoa, is cured into chali and kempu grades after weeks of husking, boiling and drying.
Selling through CAMPCO gives him a floor price, but Yellow Leaf Disease and Koleroga remain the central anxiety.
He has lost part of a harvest to Koleroga twice in the past decade, taking cooperative loans to replant.

stat.label: Arecanut CAMPCO purchased in FY2024-25, worth roughly Rs 2,825 crore

topics.label: Family & Household
topics.headline: Nuclear family of four, with an open question about the son returning
points: A tiled house on plantation land his father and grandfather worked; his elderly mother lives nearby and is visited daily.
His wife runs the drying yard, kitchen garden and cattle, and supervises the plantation when he is in Sirsi.
Their elder son works in a Bengaluru factory, visits twice a year and sends money when he can.

topics.label: Education & Schooling
topics.headline: High literacy on paper, but distance and terrain threaten Class 10
points: He stopped after SSLC because the nearest pre-university college was too far; his wife left after middle school.
Their daughter reaches a government high school by shared auto; pre-university means boarding or commuting to Sirsi.
Her mother wants her to finish secondary school and go on to a pre-university college in Sirsi.

topics.label: Health & Wellbeing
topics.headline: Monkey fever and hospitals far from the ghats
points: Kyasanur Forest Disease (monkey fever) recurs each dry season; the family avoids the forest fringe and gets vaccinated at camps.
Uttara Kannada has no medical college; serious cases mean a half-day or full-day journey out of the ghats.
Day to day they use a primary health centre a few kilometres away, and Sirsi private clinics when affordable.

topics.label: Community & Belief
topics.headline: Havyaka kinship, CAMPCO meetings and Sirsi's Marikamba Jatre
points: Havyaka Brahmin households speak Havigannada and resist being folded into a Tulu Nadu identity.
Sirsi's Marikamba Jatre, a temple festival held once every two years, is the big event for his family and neighbours.
CAMPCO's Sirsi branch and farmer meetings are a social hub for sharing news on disease, prices and schemes.

topics.label: Civic Life & Government
topics.headline: CAMPCO, Shakti buses and a grievance about district neglect
points: Uttara Kannada has no medical college and no airport, with worse roads and hospitals than Dakshina Kannada and Udupi.
The Kasturirangan Western Ghats Ecologically Sensitive Area proposals worry him over land-use restrictions on his plantation.
Panchayat talk is practical: monsoon road repair, the school building and access to the health centre.

stat.label: women use free state buses daily statewide under Shakti, since June 2023

topics.label: Worldview & Concerns
topics.headline: Distance, disease and neglect, not poverty, shape his worries
points: He frames dropout around infrequent buses, landslide-prone roads, understaffed schools and disease scares, not school fees.
He would demand a government medical college or a reliably funded referral hospital closer to Sirsi.
On arecanut he wants faster disease surveillance, subsidised replanting material and limits on cheaper imports.

schoolPressures.label: Distance & terrain
schoolPressures.detail: Pre-university colleges are in Sirsi and Siddapur; infrequent buses cross roads that wash out in monsoon.

schoolPressures.label: Seasonal disease
schoolPressures.detail: Kyasanur Forest Disease outbreak months and precaution drives can disrupt attendance.

schoolPressures.label: Thin schools
schoolPressures.detail: Government schools in smaller hamlets are more likely to be understaffed or single-teacher.

schoolPressures.label: Harvest chores
schoolPressures.detail: She helps sort and dry areca nuts after school during the harvest weeks.

female.name: The Malpe fisherman's wife
female.tagline: Mogaveera harbour worker who cures fish and runs the household while her husband is at sea.

dayInLife.text: At Malpe harbour as boats return and the catch is auctioned on the beach and in the sheds.
Sorts, salts and sun-dries fish on a cooperative plot; pay is piece-based and seasonal.
His trawler trips last several days, so she runs the household and money alone.
Does most of the cooking and childcare, and tends a small garden and a couple of hens.
Her son helps around the harbour; her daughter sometimes helps at the drying yard in holidays.

topics.label: Daily Life & Work
topics.headline: Harbour auctions, drying-yard work and a seasonal income
points: Her husband crews a mechanised trawler and can be at sea for several days at a stretch.
She belongs to the Malpe Fisherwomen's Cooperative Society, which sub-leases drying plots and supplies imported salt at a fixed price.
Income drops sharply in the monsoon fishing ban, typically June to July or August, and when diesel costs cut trips.

topics.label: Family & Household
topics.headline: She runs household decisions alone while her husband is at sea
points: A nuclear family of four in a small harbour-side house; her husband's mother lives close by and helps with childcare.
Her marriage was arranged within the Mogaveera community and she moved to her husband's family's part of Malpe.
Her son's weekend harbour work is both help and a rite of passage, but it can tip into leaving school.

topics.label: Education & Schooling
topics.headline: Fishing and drying-yard work pull at her son and daughter
points: She left school around Class 8; her husband finished SSLC but not pre-university college.
Boys are drawn into paid harbour and boat work earlier than their sisters, sometimes before Class 10 ends.
For girls, peak-season drying-yard work, commute safety and distant pre-university colleges add pressure; Shakti buses help.

topics.label: Health & Wellbeing
topics.headline: Wet, salty yard work wears her down; referrals feel uncertain
points: Standing in wet salted conditions and repetitive sorting cause skin complaints, musculoskeletal pain and fatigue she treats as routine.
Her husband faces rough weather, mechanical injury and long stretches without medical help on multi-day trawler trips.
Care runs through a government primary health centre and Udupi district hospital; serious cases go toward Mangaluru-Manipal.

topics.label: Community & Belief
topics.headline: Mogaveera kin, the fisherwomen's cooperative and local shrines
points: Mogaveera village councils were historically led by a hereditary leader called a Gurikara.
The cooperative is a mutual-support network: members share yard space, watch each other's children and swap price information.
Her ritual life centres on local shrines and boat-blessing rites before fishing reopens after the monsoon ban.

topics.label: Civic Life & Government
topics.headline: Cooperative lease, coastal rules and free bus travel
points: The cooperative leases its drying-yard land from the government and renews it with municipal and fisheries authorities.
The 2019 CRZ notification cut the No-Development Zone in crowded coastal stretches like Malpe from 200 metres to 50.
Shakti, free state bus travel for women since June 2023, is a scheme she finds unambiguously useful.

stat.label: No-Development Zone, down from 200 m, under the 2019 CRZ notification

topics.label: Worldview & Concerns
topics.headline: Enough income to keep her children in school
points: She would blame large mechanised trawlers and purse seiners for depleting near-shore stocks that artisanal fishers depend on.
She would demand guaranteed access to the Mangaluru-Manipal hospitals, not referrals withdrawn by contract disputes.
She takes pride in Malpe's harbour and the cooperative, and wants a secure long-term lease for the drying yard.

schoolPressures.label: Boat work
schoolPressures.detail: A boat owner's steady wages can pull a Class 10 boy into paid harbour work.

schoolPressures.label: Drying-yard work
schoolPressures.detail: Peak-season fish processing draws adolescent girls into paid labour.

schoolPressures.label: Thinner government schools
schoolPressures.detail: Private English-medium schools draw better-off families, leaving poorer ones in under-resourced government schools.

schoolPressures.label: Commute & safety
schoolPressures.detail: A daughter's commute to a distant pre-university college raises safety and cost worries.
